user.title: Welcome to Maxxicharge
user.description:
This setup connects your Maxxisun CCU(s) to Home Assistant via MQTT and tidies up the values.

**You will need:**
- **IP address of Home Assistant:** `{ha_ip}`. This is the “broker address” you enter at the CCU.
- **Port:** usually `1883`.
- **User and password for MQTT:** if you already have MQTT (e.g. Mosquitto) use its credentials, ideally from a dedicated MQTT-only user. Otherwise you choose them yourself in the next step for the built-in broker.
- **The Maxxisun app** (“Smart Home Integration”) or a browser in your home network.
- **CCU firmware** 2.42.103 or newer for reading, 2.43 or newer to change settings.

You do not need the CCU’s IP address, CCUs are found automatically. If Home Assistant already has MQTT I use it. Otherwise I offer a built-in broker, nothing has to be installed.

connect.title: Set up Maxxicharge
connect.description:
**How to connect the CCU to MQTT (one time):**

1. In the Maxxisun app open **Smart Home Integration** (or `http://CCU-IP/integrations/mqtt` in a browser; the page has no login, use it only in your home network).
2. Switch “MQTT connection” on. Broker address: `{broker}`, port: `{port}`.
3. Switch “Login” on and enter user and password of a Home Assistant user (ideally a dedicated MQTT-only user).
4. Save.

Requires firmware **2.42.103 or newer** (reading) and **2.43 or newer** to change settings. If the CCU is already connected just click “Submit”. The search takes up to 10 seconds.

broker_choice.description: MQTT is not set up in Home Assistant yet. You can either use the **built-in broker** (nothing to install) or set up your own MQTT.

embedded.title: Built-in MQTT broker
embedded.description: Home Assistant starts a small MQTT broker that the CCU connects to. Note user and password, you will enter them at the CCU in a moment. If port 1883 is free it is the best choice.

search.title: Connect the CCU to Home Assistant
search.description:
**At the CCU (one time):**

1. In the Maxxisun app open **Smart Home Integration** (or `http://CCU-IP/integrations/mqtt` in a browser; the page has no login, use it only in your home network).
2. Switch “MQTT connection” on. Broker address: `{broker}`, port: `{port}`.
3. Switch “Login” on. User: `{user}`, password: `{password}`.
4. Save.

Requires firmware 2.42.103 or newer (reading) and 2.43 or newer to change settings. Then click “Submit”. The search takes up to 10 seconds.

mqtt_missing.title: Set up MQTT in Home Assistant
mqtt_missing.description:
The CCU speaks MQTT, so Home Assistant needs a broker.

**No broker yet?** Install the **Mosquitto broker** add-on (Settings → Add-ons → Add-on store), start it and then open [the MQTT setup](/config/integrations/dashboard/add?domain=mqtt). Usually “Submit” is enough there.

**Already have a broker?** Set up address, port and credentials in [the MQTT setup](/config/integrations/dashboard/add?domain=mqtt).

Then click “Submit” and I will check the connection again.

no_ccu.title: No CCU found
no_ccu.description:
No new CCU announced itself on the broker. Check:

- Is the MQTT connection switched on and saved in the Maxxisun app under “Smart Home Integration” (“Connected” at the top)? Broker `{broker}`, port `{port}`.
- Are user and password correct? Rejected logins at the broker: `{rejected}` (“user” = wrong user name, “password” = wrong password). If a CCU is listed, enter user **and** password again in the Maxxisun app (do not leave it empty, otherwise the old password stays).
- Is the firmware at least 2.42.103?
- Are the CCU and Home Assistant on the same network?

After saving on the CCU it takes a few seconds until it shows up.
